summary: Procurement and security review for DeltaCare vendor onboarding. Covered MSA redlines, DPA/data residency, SLAs (uptime, latency targets), pricing approvals and next steps for SOC2 and encryption docs. Agreed to circulate redlines and schedule onboarding kickoff pending internal approvals.
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, really appreciate it. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. with me is Priya, our platform SE. How are you doing today?
00:07 Mark Rivera: Hey Jordan, good, thanks. We have Sofia from InfoSec and Tom from engineering on.
00:12 Sofia Alvarez: Hi. We'll focus on the MSA and DPA items, plus SLA details, and any security artifacts you can share.
00:18 Priya Patel: Great, thanks. Quick agenda, we'll run through the MSA redline highlights, DPA questions, SLA terms (availability targets / credits), then pricing approvals and onboarding timing. Feel free to interrupt.
00:30 Tom Nguyen: Sounds good.
00:32 Jordan Lee: First on the MSA, we saw your redlines around liability caps and data handling. We typically land on a mutual indemnity and a liability cap tied to the prior 12 months of fees. We're happy to discuss lifting for certain regulatory exposures — can you remind us of your procurement constraints?
00:52 Mark Rivera: Procurement wants a standard vendor cap, but legal is asking for higher for PHI in case of breach. There's also a requirement for audit access and stronger logging in the DPA.
01:03 Sofia Alvarez: Right, InfoSec is focused on PHI handling — encryption at rest, KMS key control, and whether Redwood's private deployment supports our VPC/on-prem options. Also need SOC2 and penetration testing cadence.
01:16 Priya Patel: Understood. For encryption, our private deployments integrate with customer KMS (we support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM setups). For hosted there is customer-key encryption option — I can share the exact KMS flow and a diagram. We have a SOC 2 Type II report and pen test summaries we can send under NDA.
01:34 Jordan Lee: Note — sometimes our transcription has Redwood Dedicated written as "red wood dedicated" in logs, haha. But on the legal side, we can add a carveout for regulatory fines and have a separate negotiation for liability cap on PHI.
01:45 Tom Nguyen: For deployment, are you able to guarantee data residency in eu-west-1? Our users in EU must keep PHI in-region.
01:52 Priya Patel: Yes, we can pin private deployment to region or we can do a VPC private offering that keeps data in eu-west-1. For hosted we have regional controls and data residency options — will share region list.
02:05 Sofia Alvarez: SLA specifics: we need 99.9% availability and an explicit credit schedule, plus latency SLOs for 95th percentile token latency — is that part of the standard SLA?
02:16 Jordan Lee: Our standard enterprise SLA starts at 99.9% with credits scaling by downtime windows; we can add latency SLOs for the dedicated plan — usually specified per model class and sequence length. We should map expected traffic and model choices to firm latency targets.
02:30 Mark Rivera: Ok — procurement will need pricing tied to committed units. If we commit to X per month we need a discount and preferred capacity. Also, pricing approver needs a final quote to sign off.
02:43 Jordan Lee: We'll send a committed capacity pricing sheet. Priya, any performance notes we should include?
02:48 Priya Patel: Yes — for generation workloads if you pick a quantized model or a smaller family we can hit sub-200ms p95 for short prompts on Dedicated GPUs; longer sequences or larger model families will change that. Also we have caching and batching options that affect cost. I'll include benchmark snapshots and the kernel/compilation notes — apologies if the auto transcript mangles KV cache to "KT cache" sometimes.
03:10 Tom Nguyen: That helps. On compliance, Sofia — will you accept SOC2 and contractual audit rights or do you need on-site audits?
03:17 Sofia Alvarez: Contractual audit rights plus periodic evidence are fine. On-site would be a stretch. We'll want a security appendix in the DPA with data deletion timelines and retention.
03:27 Jordan Lee: We can specify deletion timelines per dataset and retain logs for X days — we also provide exportable audit logs for admin review. I'll have Priya attach a sample log format.
03:36 Mark Rivera: Great. On the MSA redlines, legal flagged the termination for convenience clause and the data return obligations — they want clearer transition assistance.
03:45 Priya Patel: From an onboarding side we offer a 30-60 day transition window with export assistance. For private deployments we can provide a snapshot export to your storage.
03:55 Jordan Lee: Moving to procurement timeline — what's your internal approval cycle? Mark?
04:00 Mark Rivera: Two weeks for procurement review, legal another 7-10 days after redlines. We need pricing approved by finance, which usually adds another week. So overall 3-4 weeks if no big redlines.
04:12 Jordan Lee: Ok that aligns. We'll target sending the redlined MSA and SOC2 + encryption docs within 24-48 hours. Then Sofia can review legal redlines and we reconvene.
04:22 Tom Nguyen: One more tech Q — do you support on-prem air-gapped installs for regulated workloads?
04:27 Priya Patel: Yes, we have an on-prem package for air-gapped deployments. It requires lead time for packaging and an ops runbook; we'll include system requirements in the doc set.
04:38 Sofia Alvarez: About incident response — do you offer joint incident drills or a RTO / RPO commitment?
04:43 Jordan Lee: We have an incident management playbook, we agree on escalation contacts and can run tabletop exercises. For RTO/RPO we typically define them in the onboarding SOW.
04:55 Mark Rivera: Competitors — we're also evaluating VendorX and BigCloudAI. VendorX had lower price but no private deploy option; BigCloudAI has region support but sla was weaker.
05:08 Jordan Lee: Noted. We'll try to surface the differentiators: private deployment, KMS integration, observability, and predictable unit economics.
05:16 Tom Nguyen: For procurement, the price approver will want committed units and a price per 1k tokens or per inference.
05:23 Jordan Lee: We'll provide both models: per-token hosted pricing and committed GPU-hours for Dedicated with an effective per-inference estimate.
05:30 Priya Patel: I'll include model/quantization recommendations tied to cost/latency tradeoffs — e.g., recommend the quantized 7B variant for chat-heavy workflows vs larger 34B for high-fidelity tasks.
05:44 Sofia Alvarez: Any sample contractual language for SLAs and credits you can share?
05:48 Jordan Lee: Yes — I'll attach the standard SLA section and we can highlight fields that are negotiable.
05:53 Mark Rivera: Ok next steps — we need the redlined MSA, SOC2, encryption doc, pricing sheet. Then procurement will review and push to legal.
06:02 Jordan Lee: Great — recap of action items then: Jordan sends redlined MSA + pricing; Priya shares SOC2 + KMS flow + sample logs; Sofia reviews redlines by 9/28; Tom confirms regions by 9/30. We'll aim to schedule onboarding kickoff week of Oct 4 if approvals are in.
06:19 Sofia Alvarez: Sounds good. Anything else?
06:22 Tom Nguyen: No, thanks.
06:24 Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with the packet. Appreciate your time.
06:30 [call ends]
